page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose, 7th-generation instance driven by the AWS Nitro System. Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz across 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs without hyperthreading overhead, it offers x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 instruction set extensions. System memory consists of 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage while offering a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

In multi-core performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates high execution capability, achieving top-tier scores in stress-ng multi-core workloads, Geekbench multi-core testing, and software compilation via Clang. Cache-bound operations benefit from top-tier performance in small-block read bandwidth, while Redis SET operations reach 122.99 million operations per second. However, without integrated local NVMe storage, disk-intensive workloads rely on network storage performance.

By delivering 64 dedicated physical cores on a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, the m7a.16xlarge offers strong compute density and memory bandwidth per resource unit. This hardware profile makes it well-suited for compute-heavy parallel tasks, enterprise application backends, static web serving, software compilation pipelines, and CPU-based language model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose 7th-generation instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring a dedicated 64-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz without multithreading. It provides 256 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, along with a 25 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core execution in stress-ng and Geekbench Clang software compilation, paired with Redis SET throughput of 122.99 million operations per second. The server lacks local NVMe SSD storage and dedicated GPUs, making storage-bound workloads reliant on network-attached block storage. With 64 dedicated physical cores, the instance offers high resource density for parallel compute workloads, enterprise web application backends, software compilation pipelines, and mid-sized CPU-based language model inference.
